shared_elements: low-relief incised carving on a stone monument
horizontal band or register line framing the design
row of repeated vertical striated/hatched elements
curvilinear incised motifs on a broad surface
justification: Both surfaces carry shallow incised relief organised with a horizontal framing band above a row of repeated vertical, finely striated elements (the ribbed cap/headdress zone on the figure in A, the whole visible field in B), and both use dense parallel hatching as infill. The decisive difference is that A depicts a complete anthropomorphic figure with head, shoulders, arms and a circular chest disc set within curved bands, whereas B shows only an abstract repeating fringe-like motif with no figure, creature or relational scene at all.
